title: Electrospun Nanofiber Scaffolds with Gradations in Fiber Organization
protocol: Prepare a solution of Poly (ε-caprolactone) at an approximate concentration of 100 mg/ml.
Dissolve PCL in a mixture of dichloromethane and N,N-dimethylformamide at a ratio of 4:1 with a concentration of 10% w/v.
Place the solution in a 20 ml glass tube for mixing.
Place the glass tube into an ultrasonic cleaner for 30 minutes, or until the solution is translucent.
Add the prepared PCL solution into a 5 ml syringe with a 21 gauge blunt needle attached.
Place the syringe pump in a vertical electrospinning position.
Use a stainless steel-gap collector with an open space of 2 cm x 5 cm for the aligned fiber substrate.
Place the collector 12 cm from the needle tip.
Connect the Direct Current High Voltage power supply to the needle and ground the collector.
Ensure that the collector is individually grounded with no contact to other lab equipment.
Set the syringe pump to 1.50 ml/hr until droplets forming at the needle tip are immediately replaced when removed.
Then, set the flow rate to 0.50 ml/hr.
Turn the voltage operator to 12 kV.
Electrospin until uniaxially aligned fibers completely cover the gap on the collector.
Apply glue to the edges of a small glass plate.
Transfer fibers from the gap collector to the glass plate.
Place the glass plate on top of a grounded piece of aluminum foil of the same size.
Position the second syringe collector according to Figure 3.
Attach the plastic mask to the second syringe pump and position it 2 mm above the collector.
Add Coumarin 6 at 1% (w/w) to the PCL solution if nanoencapsulation is desired.
Mix until the solution becomes translucent.
Load the PCL or PCL/Coumarin 6 solution into a 5 ml needle with a blunt 21 gauge needle.
Set vertical pump to 0.50 ml/hr and horizontal to pull at 9 ml/hr or approximately 1 mm/min.
Electrospin until the mask has moved almost completely off the collector but with the edge area still under the mask.
Place samples on double-sided conductive tape attached to a metallic stud.
Coat samples with platinum for 40 sec using a sputter coater at 40 mA.
Examine fibers through scanning electron microscope (SEM).
Collect images at an accelerating voltage of 15 kV.
Perform fast Fourier transform (FFT) analysis on a separate fiber sample to measure fiber alignment.
Sterilize the fiber samples by soaking in a 70% ethanol solution for 2 hours.
Wash the fibers with distilled water to remove contaminants.
Culture human ADSCs in a 25 cm² flask at 37 °C under an atmosphere of 95% air/5% CO₂.
Change cell culture medium every other day.
Trypsinize the cells and count the number of cells.
Remove all culture medium from the cell culture flask.
Wash the cells with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) twice.
Add 1 ml of a pre-warmed 0.25% trypsin-EDTA solution to cover the cell monolayer.
Incubate the flask in the cell culture incubator for 2-3 minutes.
Add 4 ml of culture medium and wash out all cells from the surface by pipetting.
Centrifuge the cell suspension and re-disperse the cell pellet in the culture medium.
Count cells via hemacytometer.
Seed around 1 × 10⁴ cells to the nanofiber scaffold placed in a 35 mm culture dish.
Incubate for 3 and 7 days.
Stain cells using fluorescein diacetate (FDA) solution at 5 mg/ml.
Add 100 μl of FDA solution to the culture dish and incubate for 30 minutes.
Wash cells with PBS three times before fluorescent imaging.
Analyze cell orientation by a customized Matlab program.
